provenance: Briefly related by Larry in a short phone call with his son on August 12, 2026; noted down by his son the same day. A fragment — the full story is still to be captured. Working notes: research/interviews/2026-08-12-call-notes.md.
text: A story involving a helicopter, an explosion, and two people — the son's impression was two females or girls — with bombs around them. Larry referred to them with a word his son heard phonetically as "su-ners" (like "sooners" or "sunners").
researchNotes: The son notes he may have assumed the two were female; the word itself was Larry's. Leading hypothesis for "su-ners": SAPPERS — Viet Cong demolition commandos who infiltrated installations with explosive charges strapped to their bodies; female VC sappers are documented. The phonetic is preserved exactly as heard, and the hypothesis stays out of Larry's record until he retells the story. If confirmed, the story may correspond to a documentable sapper attack, and "sapper" joins the site glossary. Ask him to retell it: who were the two, what happened with the helicopter and the explosion, where and when.
